accuracy.evidence: Checked against the EEF guidance report Metacognition and Self-Regulated Learning (2018, updated 2021), which puts activating prior knowledge in the planning stage before monitoring and evaluation; the EYFS characteristics of effective learning (creating and thinking critically: making links, planning); Ausubel (1968) on what the learner already knows; and Ogle (1986) for the KWL chart (Know, Want to know, Learned). The race model is labelled as a model: looking first removes wrong tries up to 2 seconds, after which extra looking only adds time, which matches the adult caution about thinking so long it becomes waiting.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips teachers report when children meet new topics: I know nothing about it (prediction in step 1, tag nothing), rushing straight in (Rush lane, tag rush), thinking first is wasted time (race prediction, tag waste), thinking for ever (4 second run and tag forever), filing a statement as a wonder or a question as a know (KWL sort and tag know), linking to true but unrelated facts (I like pizza, my bike is red, tag off), and putting what I learned first (tag learned).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagthink is built around the moment before a task: a think cloud that only accepts bee facts, a two-column K and W board, a two-lane puzzle race where the child sets Sam's look-first time from 0 to 4 seconds and sees wrong tries and total time, a pick-the-helpful-memory step for new jobs, and a Stop, Think, Wonder, Start order builder. flaglink (Connecting New and Old Ideas) builds analogies between two ideas and flagsteps breaks a task into steps; neither has a think-time race or a KWL board. The shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers that they already know things by filling the think cloud themselves, finds the know versus wonder rule from the feedback (it tells, it asks), and sees from their own race runs that 0 seconds gives 4 wrong tries and 14 seconds, 2 seconds gives 0 wrong tries and 8 seconds, and 4 seconds is slower again. The done messages only name the rule after the runs.

predictions.evidence: Two locked predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: No, nothing yet for knowing about bees before a lesson (the child then fills the cloud with three bee facts), and Rush, who starts at once for who finishes first (Rush always takes 14 seconds with 4 wrong tries; Sam beats him with any look of 1 to 4 seconds). A.reveal quotes the guess in the done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with tagged wrong answers, each with its own correction: rush (Rush made 4 wrong tries), nothing (you knew bees buzz before any lesson), waste (Sam looked for 2 seconds and finished faster), forever (too long is slow too), know (it tells a thing, wonder cards ask), off (true but not about the new thing) and learned (what I learned comes at the end). Lab slips are named too, for example I like pizza is true, but it is not about bees.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short read-aloud sentences (Stop for a moment. Ask: what do I know about this?) and pass the family kid limit in validate_lessons; the adult text stays inside the family adult limit while using the precise terms prior knowledge, activating prior knowledge, metacognition, planning stage, schema and KWL chart (Know, Want to know, Learned).

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and explanation overlap with every lesson, including Connecting New and Old Ideas, Breaking Tasks into Steps and Asking Questions, is under the 12 percent limit. Each kid paragraph adds one move (stop, you know more than you think, wonder, start but not for ages); the adult paragraphs give the curriculum frame, the research and KWL, named mistakes with a caution, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots on iPhone 13 and desktop in dark and light: on the 390 px phone the canvas switches to a tall layout with the bee card and think cloud on top and memory bubbles in two columns, the K and W columns sit side by side, the race lanes span the width with five 56 px think-time circles, and every choice is repeated as a full-size button under the canvas. Nothing is clipped; long bubble text is fitted to its card width.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, every Show me completed (5 tasks) and the challenge showed. Every drag or canvas tap has a labelled button twin (Put Bees buzz in my think cloud, I know, I wonder, Sam looks first for 2 seconds, Next in my plan: Stop), and the canvas aria-label speaks each result, for example Sam looked for 2 seconds, then put every piece right: 8 seconds, the fastest!

sources: Education Endowment Foundation (2021) Metacognition and Self-Regulated Learning: guidance report
DfE (2021) Development Matters: characteristics of effective learning
Ausubel, D. P. (1968) Educational Psychology: A Cognitive View
Ogle, D. M. (1986) K-W-L: a teaching model that develops active reading of expository text, The Reading Teacher 39(6)
